content: 1. Khatlani et al. (2017) investigated the relationship between caregiver supervision practices and the risk of unintentional childhood injury mortality in Bangladesh. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. 2. Kopjar and Wickizer (1996) conducted a study comparing the safety of day care centers versus home environments in terms of injuries among children in Norway. This research was detailed in Pediatrics. 3. Kotch et al. (1997) examined the incidence of injuries among children in both home and out-of-home care settings. Their findings were published in Injury Prevention. 4. Kotch and Loda (1993) analyzed parental reports of injuries occurring at home and in child care centers among children attending such facilities. This study appeared in Early Child Development and Care. 5. Laosee et al. (2014) explored the perceptions of drowning risks among rural guardians in Thailand through a community-based household survey. The results were published in Journal of Child Health Care. 6. Lee and Kim (2019) developed a survival swimming curriculum aimed at preventing drowning, using the Delphi Method. Their work was published in the Journal of Coastal Research. 7. Leroy et al. (2012) conducted a systematic review to assess the impact of daycare programs on child health, nutrition, and development in developing countries. Their findings were published in the Journal of Development Effectiveness. 8. Liu et al. (2019) performed a case-control study in Hunan Province, China, to identify epidemiological characteristics and influencing factors of fatal drowning in children under five years old. The study was published in BMC Public Health. 9. Ma et al. (2010) analyzed risk factors for non-fatal drowning among children in rural areas of Guangdong Province, China, through a case-control study. Their findings were published in BMC Public Health. 10. Mecrow et al. (2015a) conducted a descriptive study on children reporting the rescue of other children from drowning in rural Bangladesh. This research was published in Injury Prevention. 11. Mecrow et al. (2015b) examined whether teaching children to swim increases their exposure to water or risk-taking behaviors in aquatic environments. Emerging evidence from Bangladesh was presented in Injury Prevention. 12. Moreno-Murcia et al. (2016) investigated the effect of storytelling on real and perceived aquatic competence in preschoolers. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Medicine and Sciences of Physical Activity and Sports. 13. Morrongiello et al. (2013) studied the impact of swim lesson participation on parents’ judgments of their children’s drowning risk, swimming ability, and supervision needs. This research was published in Accident Analysis and Prevention. 14. Mwaura (2008) evaluated the Madrasa preschool program in East Africa using a quasi-experimental study design. The findings were published in the International Journal of Early Years Education. 15. Nguyen and Warda (2003) discussed the benefits and considerations of swimming lessons for infants and toddlers in their article published in Paediatric and Child Health. 16. Ochoa Sangrador et al. (2007) conducted a systematic review on the relationship between child day-care attendance and acute infectious diseases. Their findings were published in the Spanish Review of Public Health. 17. Ochoa Sangrador and Vazquez Blanco (2018) reviewed the association between day-care center attendance and the risk of asthma. Their systematic review was published in Allergologia et Immunopathologia (Madrid). 18. Pando et al. (2018) conducted an observational study to inform potential drowning intervention strategies among fishing communities in Tanzania’s Lake Zone. This project report was prepared by the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine. 19. Parker et al. (1999) evaluated the effectiveness of buoyancy aids in teaching children to swim. Their findings were published in Pediatric Exercise Science. 20. Pedraza et al. (2014) studied the prevalence of infectious diseases among Brazilian preschool children attending daycare centers. Their research was published in Science and Collective Health. 21. Quan and Bennett (2006) explored attitudes, beliefs, and behaviors related to drowning and drowning prevention among Vietnamese teens and parents. Their findings were published in the Journal of Trauma: Injury, Infection, and Critical Care. 22. Rahman et al. (2010) assessed the initial community response to a childhood drowning prevention program in rural Bangladesh. Their findings were published in Injury Prevention. 23. Rahman et al. (2012) evaluated the cost-effectiveness of an injury and drowning prevention program in Bangladesh. This study was published in Pediatrics. 24. Rich and Giles (2014) examined whiteness and Euro-Canadian discourses in the Canadian Red Cross’ swim program. Their findings were published in the Journal of Sport and Social Issues. 25. Rivara et al. (1989) compared the risk of injury to children under five years of age in daycare versus home care settings. Their research was published in Pediatrics. 26. Robertson (1983) authored a book titled Injuries: Causes, Control Strategies, and Public Policy, which provides a comprehensive overview of injury prevention strategies. 27. Rosero (2012) analyzed the effectiveness of child care centers in promoting child development in Ecuador. This discussion paper was published by the Tinbergen Institute. 28. Schwebel and Brezausek (2007) investigated the role of environmental context in pediatric injury risk, focusing on home and childcare settings. Their findings were published in the Merrill-Palmer Quarterly. 29. Sellström et al. (1994) studied injuries occurring in Swedish daycare centers. Their research was published in Pediatrics. 30. Shen et al. (2016) evaluated a drowning prevention program based on testimonial videos through a randomized controlled trial. Their findings were published in the Journal of Pediatric Psychology. 31. Swyden et al. (2017) reviewed the association between childcare arrangements and overweight/obesity in preschool-aged children. Their narrative review was published in the International Journal of Obesity (London). 32. Terzidis et al. (2007) assessed age-specific changes in water safety knowledge and attitudes following a school-based intervention. Their findings were published in Injury Prevention. 33. Van Urk et al. (2014) reviewed the impact of center-based daycare for children under five years of age in high-income countries. Their systematic review was published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 34. Vanderloo (2014) conducted a systematic review on screen-viewing behaviors among preschoolers in childcare settings. The findings were published in BMC Pediatrics. 35. Vermeer and van Ijzendoorn (2006) reviewed and conducted a meta-analysis on elevated cortisol levels in children attending daycare. Their findings were published in the Early Childhood Research Quarterly. 36. The World Health Organization (2006) published guidelines for safe recreational water environments, focusing on swimming pools and similar settings. 37. The World Health Organization (2014) released a global report on drowning, emphasizing its prevention as a leading cause of unintentional injury death. 38. Yang et al. (2007) identified risk factors for childhood drowning in rural regions of a developing country through a case-control study. Their findings were published in Injury Prevention. 39. Zheng et al. (2019) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on cytomegalovirus infection prevalence in daycare centers. Their findings were published in Reviews in Medical Virology. 40. Zoritch et al. (2000) reviewed the impact of daycare for preschool children. Their findings were published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews.
